Thirty years I've been farming this land. I know what works here in Quzhou — the soil, the timing, the water table. My sons help sometimes but they've got jobs in the city now, so I can't waste labor or money on things that don't pay.

My main rotation is wheat then maize — that's what this land is for. Those two crops fill about 25 mu. I keep 6.5 mu aside for zucchini because it sells well at the local market and gives me cash income when the grain prices are bad.

**Wheat:** I plant in October. I use the improved varieties — Jimai 22 or similar, whatever the seed station recommends this year. Thirty years tells me it yields reliably. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble. Irrigation here is necessary — I pump four times: before sowing to settle the soil, again in winter to protect the roots from frost heave, at jointing, and at heading when the grain is forming. Fertilizer I split — base and topdress. I spray twice for weeds and once for powdery mildew in spring.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I go in with direct seeding — no-tillage saves me time and the soil moisture stays. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 has been good to me. Three irrigations: at sowing, tasseling, and grain fill. I apply nitrogen in two shots — base and one topdress at V6. Pest pressure is manageable, usually just one herbicide pass and one for corn borer.

**Zucchini:** I plant this in April on the separate 6.5 mu plot. It's labor-intensive but the margins are better than grain. Hybrid seed, rotary tillage before planting. Zucchini drinks water — I irrigate every week or two throughout the season, roughly ten times. Powdery mildew hits hard so I spray five times: fungicide rotations I learned the hard way.
